briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the Climate Briefing for November 15, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deadlock at COP31 and Global Warnings of Climate Catastrophe
sections.content: Following the hottest summer on record since observations began in 1850, the global death toll from extreme weather events in 2026 has already reached tens of thousands [69]. In response, UN Secretary-General António Guterres strongly urged immediate and drastic emission reductions and the protection of vulnerable communities to avert a climate disaster [60, 61]. The UN also warned that millions could be displaced and forced to relocate due to the impacts of climate change [51, 63]. However, the COP31 summit held in Antalya, Türkiye, is facing an impasse over disagreements regarding fossil fuels, while thousands of protesters on site and the UN climate chief demand a swift agreement and decisive action [50, 53, 54].

sections.title: 🌱 Projected Surge in Global Renewable Energy and Industrial Infrastructure Expansion
sections.content: With fossil fuel security concerns accelerating the energy transition, global carbon emissions have shown a downward trend this year for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic [12]. Driven by energy security, worldwide renewable energy capacity is projected to surge to 4,800 GW [33]. Domestically, the South Korean government is pursuing an investment of 2.8 trillion won in renewable energy financing and deployment support [31]. In line with this, major corporations such as LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI are participating in North America's largest renewable energy exhibition, accelerating their technological push into the AI data center power market [32, 38].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 South Korea Showcases Ocean, Food, and Industrial Carbon-Neutral Innovations at COP31
sections.content: The South Korean government and industry are presenting multifaceted carbon reduction solutions at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye [2, 20]. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea participated in the summit to highlight achievements in addressing the climate crisis through marine initiatives and to explore international cooperation on blue carbon [1, 3, 5]. Following the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry delegation's promotion of industrial carbon-neutral innovations, a framework agreement on climate change cooperation between South Korea and Nepal was signed, expanding the foundation for international mitigation projects [9, 20]. In addition, Pulmuone garnered attention at COP31 by presenting research findings demonstrating a 30% reduction in carbon emissions achieved through dietary transitions [4, 11].

sections.title: ⚠️ Climate Crisis Hits Dining Tables as Local Governments Fall Short of Emission Reduction Targets
sections.content: The repercussions of climate change are posing a tangible threat to food prices and ecosystems as a whole [13, 55]. Domestically, dietary impacts have become visible as prices for imported Norwegian mackerel soared due to the disappearance of key local marine species [13], while abroad, rare dead-wood moss species in Türkiye face an extinction crisis due to the 'summit trap' phenomenon [55]. However, greenhouse gas reductions across South Korea's 17 metropolitan and provincial governments—a key pillar of crisis response—reached only about 90% of their target last year [29]. As climate damage grows increasingly widespread, it is urgent to establish practical and rigorous implementation oversight measures at the local government level.

briefing.closing: As the climate crisis manifests into tangible real-world damage, swift consensus within the international community alongside decisive action to fulfill domestic emission reduction targets are urgently required. This concludes today's Climate Briefing.
